mechanism_narrative: The abrupt one-week collapse in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility reflects an emergent closure/distancing policy regime that will continue suppressing discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks as restrictions persist or tighten further.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell to -21.1 at t-0w from -0.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages higher than the last 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining depressed.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility at t-0w (5.9, up from 0.4 the prior week) indicates households shifting to stay-at-home behavior, which mechanically reduces time available for retail and recreation visits over the following weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 0.4 to 5.9 week over week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds upward over the next 2 weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues to rise or stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden single-week drop in TRANSIT mobility exceeding 20 points signals a stockpiling-then-withdrawal behavioral pattern: people front-load grocery/pharmacy trips while avoiding retail and recreation venues, deepening the RETAIL_REC decline over the next week before any stabilization.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -2.7 to -22.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not continue falling in the week immediately following a greater-than-20-point TRANSIT drop.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility turning negative (-1.3) after three weeks of positive values suggests outdoor substitution activity is also contracting, removing a potential offset channel and reinforcing an overall contraction in out-of-home discretionary activity including retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 7.1 to -1.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS and RETAIL_REC decouple such that PARKS stays negative while RETAIL_REC recovers upward over the next 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The joint collapse of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT in the same week as RETAIL_REC's drop indicates a common shock (reduced commuting) that mechanically removes incidental retail trips tied to commute paths; as long as both remain suppressed together, RETAIL_REC will stay low, but if WORKPLACES recovers while TRANSIT stays low, incidental retail decline may partially reverse.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 2.4 to -13.1 and TRANSIT fell from -2.7 to -22.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain jointly depressed.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues an uptrend (from -2.1 to 8.1 over four weeks) while RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT fall, this divergence signals a selective-essential-only mobility regime driven by policy guidance; this pattern will persist and keep RETAIL_REC suppressed for the next 4 weeks as long as the divergence between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC widens.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC gap widens beyond 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 8.1 while RETAIL_REC fell to -21.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: The GROCERY_PHARM-RETAIL_REC gap narrows over the next 4 weeks while RETAIL_REC still declines, or the gap widens but RETAIL_REC rises.

mechanism_narrative: Early-to-mid March marks the seasonal transition toward spring outdoor activity; absent the current disruption, rising PARKS mobility in prior weeks (10.7, 2.1, 7.1) would normally presage seasonal upticks in nearby retail and recreation visits, but this baseline seasonal lift is now being overridden by the acute week-0 shock.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged positive values of 10.7, 2.1, 7.1 over the prior three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 4 weeks despite the historical seasonal pattern of rising spring outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 5 points while WORKPLACES simultaneously falls below -10, the combination indicates a decisive shift to home-centered living (remote work plus reduced outside errands), compounding to further depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 5 and WORKPLACES < -10 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 5.9 and WORKPLACES reached -13.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 4 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 5 and WORKPLACES staying below -10.
